Consider a function $f(t)$ for which the graph of the Laplace transform $L{f(t)}=F(s)$ is shown above. Which of the following could be the graph of $L{{e}^{-6t}f(t)}?$
worked_solution:
The first shifting theorem states that if
$L{f(t)}=F(s),$
then
$L{{e}^{at}f(t)}=F(s-a).$

This implies that multiplying a function $f(t)$ by ${e}^{at}$ shifts the corresponding Laplace transform horizontally along the $s$-axis.

- If $a>0,$ the graph of $F(s)$ shifts to the right.

- If $a<0,$ the graph of $F(s)$ shifts to the left.

In our case, to get the graph of $L{{e}^{-6t}f(t)},$ we must shift the graph of $F(s)$ by $6$ units to the left.
